title: Do You Need a New Co-Manufacturer?
summary: If you’re contemplating switching your contract manufacturer, here’s how to know it’s time and what the process looks like.
body_markdown:

November 5, 2026


Every consumer packaged goods brand experiences growing pains at some time in their product journey. At The Fresh Factory, what we see most often is the brand whose co-manufacturer can’t scale with them. And while switching co-manufacturers is an arduous process, it makes sense if it ultimately increases efficiency, capacity, and your sales.


If you’re contemplating switching your co-man, here’s how to know it’s time and what the process looks like.


## Signs a Co-Manufacturer Can’t Scale with You


The common reasons brands leave a current co-manufacturer to work with The Fresh Factory include:


- **Capacity:** The co-manufacturer lacks the capacity a brand needs to meet orders or accept limited time offers and rotational business.
- **Efficiency:** Food production is inefficient, because the co-manufacturer doesn’t have the right equipment. “A lot of times, the way they’re producing is what they needed to do to start the business,” says Donna Duwe, Executive Vice President at The Fresh Factory. “But it’s not efficient, and until they’re able to grow efficiently, their pricing is going to stay higher than necessary.”
- **Certifications:** The brand is receiving interest from larger retailers that require[certifications](https://thefreshfactory.co/certifications/) the facility doesn’t hold, like SQF, organic, and Non-GMO. “As you grow, you need to have all of these boxes checked,” Duwe says.


## When to Switch Co-Manufacturers


The signs above are obvious reasons to make a switch, but ideally you’ll start the process before it becomes a fire alarm. The process of switching co-manufacturers can take up to six months, so you don’t want to wait until you’ve secured a region of Costco and can’t fulfill the order.


If a contract manufacturer is inhibiting growth, it’s time to evaluate other options.


“Most brands recognize when they’ve gotten all they can out of their contract manufacturer, and they start looking proactively,” Duwe says.


## The Process of Switching Co-Manufacturers


Getting your SKUs in production with a new manufacturer typically takes between three to six months. A single product with straightforward packaging moves faster than a multi-SKU line with specialized formats or certification requirements.


You can speed things up by having key information ready before you reach out to a new partner:


- Product specifications
- Ingredient deck
- Packaging specs and label files
- Retail commitments and delivery dates
- Current production volumes


When making a switch, you’re moving a product that already has customers, retail commitments, and a flavor and texture consumers expect. The goal is to improve how the product is made without changing what people love about it.


A recipe that runs one way on your current co-manufacturer’s equipment may need adjustments to perform the same way on new machinery.


“There are always a lot of details to work through,” says Bill Besenhofer, Co-founder and CEO of The Fresh Factory. “Every production line is different, and every person who runs a machine is different. There’s no such thing as plug and play.”


Expect trial runs, taste testing, and some back and forth before production is fully dialed in. To keep product on shelves during that time, plan to build extra inventory with your current co-manufacturer before you give notice. Many brands also overlap production for a period, so the new facility is fully up and running before the old one stops.


The process becomes more complicated when the old co-manufacturer owns the recipe. That’s where in-house research and development becomes critical. The Fresh Factory’s experienced[food scientists](https://thefreshfactory.co/blog/research-development-phase/) help brands successfully reinvent their product based on ingredient decks.


## Find the Right Partner


Because switching co-manufacturers takes valuable production time, it’s important to find the right partner. Before you sign with a new manufacturer, make sure they can solve the problems that pushed you to leave in the first place. Here’s what to evaluate:


- Capacity to support your growth
- Certifications
- Equipment and fill methods that fit your product
- In-house R&D to match or recreate your formula
- Clear formula ownership terms
- Ingredient standards that align with your brand


The Fresh Factory knows switching co-manufacturers is disruptive. To ease the transition, our team works through the details with you, from trial runs to packaging and scale-up. And we make sure you own what we create together.


“There are very few formulas in our playbook that are owned by The Fresh Factory alone,” Duwe says. “Our customers pay for the R&D work so they can own their products. Does that allow them to leave us? Yes. But if we’re doing our job, they shouldn’t want to.”


If your current co-manufacturer is limiting your growth,[contact The Fresh Factory](https://thefreshfactory.co/contact/) to talk through what a transition could look like for your brand.
